title: Per-Mission-Type Reward Overrides
doc: CKF Hard Mode - per-mission-type reward overrides.
One entry per MissionTypeId. Blank slots do nothing. Slots use the
adjustment syntax MissionRewards.cs:392-414 parses:
""     leave the game's value alone
"=40"  set it to 40
"+25"  add 25 to whatever the mission shipped with
"-25"  subtract 25
"x1.5" multiply it   ("*1.5" is the same thing)
Anything else is logged as unparseable and ignored.
BonusPayment and BonusExperience are PERCENTAGES applied to the base reward
curve, not credit amounts. PowerLevelBonus shifts the mission level. Those
three are edited on the MissionRequestModel before the game does its own
arithmetic, so they take effect when a mission is generated.
ObjectivePayment scales the mission's OWN cash terms - the per-file and
per-target payments that carry no goal, no turn limit and no alarm ceiling,
measured at 30% of the full job payment each (MissionRewards.cs:220-231,
272-276). SecondaryPayment scales CONDITIONAL cash rewards, the generated
bonuses like 'finishing in 14 turns'. Both are the same RewardTypeId, which
is why they get separate levers: without the split you could not raise what
a Kill3 pays per target without inflating every generated turn-limit bonus
attached to it. A row's 'Lever' field in the reference data says which of the
two reaches it (scripts/refresh_mission_roster.py:270).
NEITHER SLOT REACHES A NON-CASH SECONDARY OBJECTIVE. Both act only on reward
rows whose RewardTypeId is 7 or 13, the two cash types; a Blueprint, File,
Influence or NBSCubes row is left alone, because scaling RewardQuantity there
would multiply the number of blueprints (MissionRewards.cs:191-208). The
top-level 'secondaryObjectives' block lists exactly those non-cash goals and
nothing in the plugin reads it.
There is no pattern-bucket layer. The PureCombatTypes / SoloHackTypes lists
and their bonus knobs were removed in 2.11.0; an exact
MissionTypeId entry is the only way to reach a mission type.
The five slot columns - BonusPayment, BonusExperience, PowerLevelBonus,
ObjectivePayment and SecondaryPayment - carry "format": "adjust", the
adjustment grammar Adjust.Parse reads (MissionRewards.cs:392-415) and
LoadOverrides applies to exactly those five and to no other column
(MissionRewards.cs:325-329). 'type' and 'note' are plain strings.
The reward stack is two layers with no overlap: the "rewardcurve" section
sets the base per power level, this section adjusts one mission type.
REGENERATING THE ROSTER. scripts/refresh_mission_roster.py rewrites this
file after a play session. A 'shipped' value of null means that mission type
has not been generated in a captured session yet, and a refresh fills it in.
As the script stands it preserves your override slots, your // comment lines
above an entry, and any JSON key it does not itself generate, and it refuses
to write at all rather than lose a comment (refresh_mission_roster.py:154-
191, 464-467). The GUI's save path ends both of
those guarantees: a hand-added comment or an unrecognised key is dropped.
REFERENCE KEYS THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT OWN. 'shipped', 'roomFlags',
'objectivePayments' and the top-level 'secondaryObjectives' block are
annotations. The plugin deserialises none of them (MissionRewards.cs:261-263;
nothing else in the source or scripts/ names the other three), so editing one
changes no reward. They are not schema fields, no generator writes them, and
the GUI must not offer them for editing. 'shipped' is already inconsistent
with itself - the same column appears as ExpMod in 9 entries and
ExperienceMod in 16 - and the dump plugin's CSV is
canonical: regenerate these from it or drop them. Until then, read them as
undated notes, not as the game's current values.
REMOVED, 2026-09-01: a closing line reading 'Generated from
schema/missionrewards.schema.json.' It was the footer of the sidecar
header comment this doc used to be written into, and it named this file as
the place to edit instead of the comment. The sidecars are pure JSON now
and nothing writes a comment into one, so the line described an origin the
text it followed no longer has.
uiDoc: Changes what one type of job pays. Each row is a single mission type, matched by name. There is no wildcard, so reaching a whole family means listing every type in it. A slot left empty keeps the game's default values.

The game writes these numbers RELATIVE to 100% payment. =40 means 140% of the Baseline Reward Curve. +25 and -25 adds or removes 25% from the game's default for that mission, whatever it was. x1.5 multiplies the default data. Any other formatting is ignored and noted in the log.
Power Level Bonus shifts the mission's level but I'm not certain what that does exactly. All three are applied while a mission is being built.

Objective Payment applies to sub-primary objectives like Loot 3 Files or Kill 3 Captains. Secondary Payment scales fully-optional objectives like finishing inside a turn limit or keeping security level low.
Non-cash rewards like blueprints, files, influence, and NBS cubes are unaffected.

fields.label: Mission type overrides
fields.uiDoc: One row per mission type, matched exactly and case-insensitively. A type listed twice is warned about and the later entry wins. A row with every slot blank changes nothing. Setting to 0 means paying 100% of the baseline mission reweard. Most proc-gen missions default to -20% XP for example.
fields.doc: One row per MissionTypeId, matched exactly and case-insensitively - there is no pattern layer, so a family is reached one type at a time. A type listed twice is warned about and the later entry wins. A row with every slot blank is inert. The shipped file groups its entries into five families, which are an editorial aid to reading rather than anything the plugin acts on: story and other non-procedural types (no PGen in the key, or an _M<n> series marker, or a row in MissionModel - hand-authored, often NoPayment); Power Play types (PowerPlay in the key); solo hacks (MaxCharacters 1); pure-combat types (Battle in the key, with RoomFlagTypes.FullCombat as the authoritative test); and everything else, where combat may still happen but a quiet route exists. [unverified: the MissionModel, MaxCharacters and RoomFlagTypes tests behind that grouping are read off game dumps that are not in this repository, and the solo-hack group is measured only where marked and inferred from the key otherwise - scripts/refresh_mission_roster.py:109-110 states that caveat and family() at :135-139 implements it, taking MaxCharacters 1 where a shipped value exists and falling back to the key otherwise.] CITATION CORRECTION, 2026-08-31: that caveat was cited as ckf.hardmode.missions.json:294 until the sidecar comment strip removed the section banner that line held, leaving a citation to a line that no longer exists. The banners were generated from refresh_mission_roster.py's FAMILIES table and were never hand-written (that table), so the wording did not move out of the repository - the citation was pointing at the copy rather than the source. CORRECTION, 2026-08-31: this field carried "keyedBy": "type", which says the block is a JSON object keyed by the type. It is not, and never was: the file on disk is a JSON array, and MissionRewards.cs:297-298 declares `[JsonPropertyName("missions")] public List<MissionOverride> Missions`, deserialised at :318, so an object here would break the plugin's read outright. The keyedBy has been dropped; the array is the truth. How it came to be written is not recorded anywhere in this repository and is not guessed at here. [measured: MissionRewards.cs:297-298, 318-320; ckf.hardmode.missions.json "missions" is a 70-element JSON array]
